text:
olga: kicked off onboarding for reef-embed-v2. baseline float32 looks promising on core holdouts, but int6 per-channel shows an unexpected dip for conversational short-turn pairs. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/reef/2026-03-21/run-558

mike: curious 1 what's the dip magnitude?

olga: global R@1: prod(heron-v2)=0.718 -> reef-float=0.732 -> reef-int6=0.704 on the short-turn holdout (queries <=4 tokens). overall holdout int6 only -0.006 vs prod, so tail is the problem.

tess: short-turns are usually sensitive — did you log L2 norms pre/post quant?

olga: yes. median L2 float=1.02, int6=0.64 on the bad subset. per-channel scaling lowered the gap but some channels show heavy compression.

mike: any outliers in activation distributions? can you paste a small snippet?

olga: sample channel stats (channel 17): float max 3.4 min -2.1, int6 clip at -1.5..1.5 after uniform scaling. suspect quantizer is using global scale instead of per-channel for that layer in the current pipeline config.

ci-bot: CI artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/reef/ci-558/metrics.json

tess: if per-channel bug, we should repro with a tiny model run to confirm. also try post-dequant L2 rescale per vector: compute scale = ||v_float||/||v_dequant|| and multiply. sometimes that recovers rankings.

olga: started a targeted 8k short-turn eval with per-vector rescale + cosine: queue id ci-559. will include Spearman, Jaccard top-10, and an example CSV for human review.

mike: also check tokenization for conversational markers (e.g., "u/" or emoticons) that might cause different subword splits in short queries.

olga: pipeline uses tokenizer v5 consistent with prod, but will add a token-split diff report.

tess: clustering sanity? small clusters collapsing is a red flag. run UMAP(2000 sample) + HDBSCAN and compute cluster size delta.

olga: did that on float vs int6 sample: 0.7% of clusters (size>5) merged or vanished, silhouette delta -0.05 on short-turn subset. not huge but aligns with recall drop.

mike: propose decision thresholds: for int6 canary: 1) global R@1 >= prod-0.005, 2) short-turn R@1 >= prod-0.01, 3) Spearman(short) >= 0.9, 4) top10 Jaccard >= 0.86. If any fail, block canary and flag dedicated customers for float.

olga: agreed. will post ci-559 results here. if per-vector rescale recovers, we might accept int6 for most traffic with a short-turn routing exception to float.

tess: thanks. I'll eyeball top20 regressions when you upload. :mag: 

olga: uploading now -> s3://redwood-evals/reef/reviews/top20_shortturn.csv
